stubs.angle: Which of several ways to write a test that checks a discount for many inputs follows the guidance against logic such as if, loops and computed expectations inside a test body?
stubs.answerHinge: A test with branches, loops or an expected value computed by the same formula as the production code can hide its own bug, so expectations should be literal values and cases should be separate tests or parameterized rows.

stubs.angle: A hand-written ExpectThrows helper calls an async method that throws ArgumentException but prints FAIL: no exception; find the line in the helper that lets the exception escape notice.
stubs.answerHinge: The helper invokes the Func<Task> without awaiting it, and an async method stores its exception in the returned task, so the helper must await the task (as Assert.ThrowsAsync does) to observe the exception.

stubs.angle: How do you give a class that depends on HttpClient canned HTTP responses in a unit test without a network call?
stubs.answerHinge: HttpClient's send methods are not virtual, so you construct a real HttpClient over a test HttpMessageHandler whose overridden SendAsync returns the canned HttpResponseMessage.

stubs.angle: Which statements about Playwright for .NET actionability checks and web-first assertions are true when replacing Thread.Sleep in browser end-to-end tests?
stubs.answerHinge: Playwright actions wait for the element to be actionable and Expect assertions retry until the condition holds or the timeout expires, so fixed sleeps are unnecessary and make tests both slower and flakier.

stubs.angle: A test of a background consumer polls with a WaitUntil helper and prints PASS although the consumer never processes the message; find the defective line in the helper.
stubs.answerHinge: The polling helper simply returns when the timeout elapses instead of failing, so the test passes without the condition ever becoming true; a wait-for-condition helper must throw or fail on timeout.

stubs.angle: Why is mocking a third-party SDK client directly in unit tests risky, and what structure do you use instead?
stubs.answerHinge: A mock of a type you do not own encodes your assumptions about its behaviour, so you wrap the SDK in your own narrow adapter interface, mock or fake that interface, and cover the adapter with integration tests against the real dependency.

stubs.angle: How do outside-in and inside-out TDD differ in where you start and how you use test doubles, and when would you choose each?
stubs.answerHinge: Outside-in starts from a failing acceptance test and uses mocks to discover the interfaces of collaborators top-down, while inside-out builds and state-verifies the core units first and composes them later, trading design discovery against coupling of tests to interactions.

stubs.angle: Which techniques make a test of an asynchronous message consumer deterministic instead of relying on sleeps?
stubs.answerHinge: The test should wait on an explicit completion signal such as a TaskCompletionSource set by the code or a fake, bounded with Task.WaitAsync(timeout), rather than on Thread.Sleep, Task.Delay or blocking .Result calls.

stubs.angle: How do you test endpoints protected by [Authorize] with WebApplicationFactory without a real identity provider?
stubs.answerHinge: In ConfigureTestServices you register a test AuthenticationHandler scheme that issues a ClaimsPrincipal with the needed claims and make it the default scheme, so the real authorization policies still run.

stubs.angle: The team must change billing rules in an old module that has no tests and tangled dependencies, and a bug would cost money; how do you lead the work?
stubs.answerHinge: First pin current behaviour with characterization tests at a seam you can reach, break dependencies with minimal safe refactorings, then change behaviour test-first, instead of either rewriting blindly or editing without a safety net.

stubs.angle: A browser end-to-end suite now takes two hours and gates every pull request, so developers batch changes and wait; what do you do as tech lead?
stubs.answerHinge: Push most checks down to unit and integration tests that verify the same rules faster, keep only a thin set of critical-journey end-to-end tests on the gate, and run the rest on a schedule, because end-to-end tests are the most expensive way to find a defect.

stubs.angle: Part of the team wants to make TDD mandatory for all code and the rest objects; how do you decide and introduce it?
stubs.answerHinge: TDD is a skill whose benefit depends on context, so a lead grows it through pairing, katas and pilot areas where it fits and judges it by outcomes such as defect rates and design feedback, rather than mandating test-first for every line or policing it by a metric.

stubs.angle: Dozens of teams write their own fakes of a shared platform service and their tests pass while production breaks; how do you organise test doubles across the organisation for years?
stubs.answerHinge: The owning team ships an official in-memory fake together with the client library and runs the same contract test suite against both the fake and the real service, so the fake cannot silently drift and consumers stop maintaining divergent copies.
